claims.title: Conflicting finality implies a slashed quorum intersection
claims.statement: In the abstract model, a finalization fork implies q_intersection_slashed: there exist two quorums whose shared validators are all slashable.

details: A finite validator type with decidable equality; a hash type with decidable equality; threshold, stake, validator-set, parent, genesis and state parameters.
The hypothesis finalization_fork contains two finalized blocks with mutual non-ancestry. Justification derivations encode the quorum links.
Transitive dependencies and axioms have not been completely audited by the atlas. The proof assistant, libraries and recorded model remain part of the trust boundary.

limitations: Structural result only: it does not assert that the shared set is nonempty or has positive weight.
Not a proof of Fulu state-transition conformance, deployed clients, signatures, network delivery or production accountable-safety thresholds.

claims.title: Post-genesis checkpoints stay unchanged or move strictly forward
claims.statement: A successful Lean model transition with a nonzero latest block-header slot leaves each justified/finalized checkpoint unchanged, including its root, or replaces it at a strictly greater slot.

details: State.transition s b = .ok s'.
The pre-state latestBlockHeader.slot is not zero; genesis anchoring is excluded.
Transitive dependencies and axioms have not been completely audited by the atlas. The proof assistant, libraries and recorded model remain part of the trust boundary.

limitations: Does not establish checkpoint ancestry across branches.
The Lean transition model is the subject, not the Python leanSpec implementation. The manual correspondence is not a refinement proof.

claims.title: Honestly generated KZG openings satisfy the pairing equation
claims.statement: For a coefficient vector, a generated power SRS and an evaluation point, KZG.correctness shows that the model's generated opening verifies for the polynomial's evaluation.

details: Prime p; prime-order groups G1, G2 and Gt with the module and equality structures in the theorem; the group order (Nat.card G1 = p) is carried by the PrimeOrderWith class instances, not an explicit theorem hypothesis after upstream #1468.
A bilinear pairing, generators, degree parameter n, SRS secret a, coefficient vector and evaluation point z, under the recorded Lean definitions.
Transitive dependencies and axioms have not been audited for this revision.

limitations: Algebraic correctness is not binding, knowledge soundness, ceremony security or zero knowledge.
Generic single-point coefficient-form opening, not Ethereum's batched cell verifier, blob encoding, BLS12-381 implementation or a deployed prover.

claims.title: An accepted SSZ decode re-encodes to its own input
claims.statement: For every well-formed type declaration of the Lean SSZ model (booleans, unsigned integers, byte vectors, byte lists, bit vectors, bit lists, progressive bit lists, vectors, lists, progressive lists, fixed-height and progressive containers, and compatible unions), a successful decode re-encodes to its own input: serialize_of_deserialize proves serialize shape value = .ok data from deserialize shape data = .ok value and shape.wellFormed = .ok ().

details: The declaration shape is well formed (shape.wellFormed = .ok ()) and decoding succeeded for the input bytes.
Encoding and decoding are the model functions of EthLib.Consensus.Ssz; canonicality is stated inside that model and is not checked against external conformance vectors.
Transitive dependencies and axioms have not been completely audited by the atlas. The proof assistant, libraries and recorded model remain part of the trust boundary.

limitations: Model-scoped: no correspondence theorem to the Python consensus-specs codec, the ssz-specs reference implementation or production client code; the recorded relationship is a manual comparison.
Covers decoded acceptance; it does not analyse network framing, persistence, partial reads or any client runtime beyond the pure byte-level model.

The atlas review compared the recorded top-level theorem and its local proof body; Lean has not been replayed and transitive dependencies and axioms are not audited. The converse directions (decoding a re-encoded value, and total rejection of non-canonical inputs) are stated by the same module family but are not separately evidenced by this intake.

claims.title: A constructed SSZ branch rebuilds the value's hash-tree root
claims.statement: For a successfully rooted value of the Lean SSZ model (hashTreeRoot shape value = .ok root), branch construction for any readable generalised index returns a branch that rebuilds the root: buildProof_rebuilds_value_root proves calculateMerkleRootUnchecked leaf branch index = .ok root from nodeRoot shape value index = .ok leaf and getBranchIndices index = .ok indices.

details: hashTreeRoot succeeds for the value and the target index names a readable node; branch indices derive via getBranchIndices.
The Merkle tree is the model's per-index node function with a MerkleTree predicate; the combine operation (the underlying hash) is an opaque parameter of the model.
Transitive dependencies and axioms have not been completely audited by the atlas. The proof assistant, libraries and recorded model remain part of the trust boundary.

limitations: Model-scoped consensus Merkleization with generalised indexes; not an analysis of gossipsub delivery, light-client sync or the execution-layer Patricia trie.
No collision-resistance or hash-security statement: the combine parameter is abstract, so the result is structural.
The atlas review compared the recorded top-level theorem and its local proof body; Lean has not been replayed and transitive dependencies and axioms are not audited.

claims.title: Varint encoding round-trips and accepted prefixes are canonical
claims.statement: For every leanp2p UVarint value and suffix, decoding its encoding followed by that suffix returns the value and untouched suffix. Every successful decode consumes exactly the canonical encoding of its returned value.

details: UVarint carries a value below 2^63; encode and decode? operate on List Nat.
The accepted-input direction assumes decode? succeeds. The decoder enforces minimal encodings and a nine-byte budget.
Local statements and proof bodies were inspected. A complete transitive dependency and axiom audit was not performed.

limitations: The 63-bit, nine-byte codec does not cover the full 64-bit, ten-byte range required by Beacon Req/Resp and used by Lean Spec framing.
Beacon requires support for the full Uint64 range and only recommends minimal encodings; leanp2p rejects non-minimal encodings. This is not codec conformance.
No ByteArray adapter, Snappy decompression, Gossipsub correctness, transport security or network liveness is proved here.

claims.title: Conflicting k-finality yields a churn-adjusted intersection bound
claims.statement: For two mutually non-ancestral k-finalized blocks, the model constructs validator subsets qL and qR whose intersection weight is at least max(wt(VL) - activationL - exitR, wt(VR) - activationR - exitL) minus the two one-third residuals. All subtraction is truncated Nat subtraction, relative to a reference validator set.

details: Two k-finalization hypotheses and mutual non-ancestry; a reference block supplies the reference validator set.
Finite validators, Nat-valued stake, abstract parent links, validator sets and a Threshold instance.
Local statements and proof bodies were inspected. A complete transitive dependency and axiom audit was not performed.

limitations: The lower bound can be zero; no unconditional positive slashed weight or one-third stake loss is asserted.
The theorem conclusion retains subset witnesses and the weight inequality, not a slashing predicate; the existing structural accountable-safety claim is separate.
No conformance to Beacon epoch, balance, churn or penalty implementation rules is established.

claims.title: Equivalent vote tallies select the same LMD-GHOST head
claims.statement: If the start root resolves to an anchor and a maintained weight map is pointwise equal to the full ancestor tally, the Lean GHOST walk using that map selects exactly the head returned by computeLmdGhostHead, including the threshold filter and tie-break.

details: The start root must resolve to an anchor block.
Weights.Equiv requires the maintained map to equal accumulateAncestorWeights at every root.
Local statements and proof bodies were inspected. A complete transitive dependency and axiom audit was not performed.

limitations: This is a theorem within the Lean store model, not a refinement proof about the Python specification or a production client.
The model walk uses st.blocks.length + 1 fuel; a full correspondence to the Python while-loop is not established.
Correct incremental maintenance, removed-vote handling and proto-array best-child caches are not proved by this theorem.

claims.title: KZG evaluation-binding advantage reduces to t-SDH
claims.statement: For each evaluation-binding adversary in the ArkLib KZG game, its probability of producing conflicting valid openings is at most the t-SDH success probability of the constructed bindingReduction.

details: Prime-order groups and the recorded bilinear pairing/module structure.
The pairing of the chosen generators is nonzero; games use the specified private uniform-sampling semantics.
Local statements and proof bodies were inspected. A complete transitive dependency and axiom audit was not performed.

limitations: This reduction does not prove t-SDH hardness or a concrete negligible advantage; the reduced success probability can be large.
The separate binding corollary requires a hardness assumption over an explicit adversary class containing the reduction.
No refinement to Fulu batched cell proofs, concrete curve encodings, trusted-setup secrecy or deployed verifier code is established.

claims.title: BLS hash-to-G2 succeeds with a nonsingular curve point
claims.statement: For every message and domain-separation byte array, the EthLib hashToG2 function returns a point satisfying G2.Valid, the nonsingularity predicate on the BLS12-381 twist.

details: The statement concerns EthLib hashToG2 and its fixed BLS12-381 field and curve definitions.
Local statements and proof bodies were inspected. A complete transitive dependency and axiom audit was not performed.

limitations: Curve membership is not prime-order subgroup membership, signature verification correctness or unforgeability.
No refinement to the Beacon BLS implementation or proof of the full ciphersuite is established.

claims.title: Generated leanXMSS keys verify successfully produced signatures
claims.statement: If keyGen returns a secret/public-key pair and sign succeeds for a leaf index and message, EthLib verify accepts that signature under the generated public key.

details: keyGen seed must return the recorded key pair, and sign succeeds with .ok signature.
The theorem uses the EthLib Keccak-based, two-layer leanXMSS model and its typed messages and leaf indices.
Local statements and proof bodies were inspected. A complete transitive dependency and axiom audit was not performed.

limitations: EthLib uses Keccak-256 and WOTS+C in a two-layer height-16 draft; the selected Lean Spec uses a Poseidon-based generalized XMSS scheme with different parameters.
Signing success is a hypothesis; the theorem does not bound grinding failure or prove unforgeability.
Leaf-index reuse prevention, state management, signature aggregation and equivalence to the selected Lean Spec are not proved.

claims.title: Encoding and decoding a KZG cell preserves its field elements
claims.statement: For an EthLib CosetEvals array containing exactly FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_CELL (64) BLS scalar-field elements, cellToCosetEvals (cosetEvalsToCell ys) returns .ok ys.

details: The array has exactly 64 elements of the typed BLS12-381 scalar field.
Local statements and proof bodies were inspected. A complete transitive dependency and axiom audit was not performed.

limitations: This is a cell serialization theorem, not correctness or binding of KZG proof verification.
It does not prove Reed-Solomon recovery, PeerDAS sampling availability, arbitrary-input acceptance or Python/client conformance.

claims.title: MODEXP computation returns modular exponentiation
claims.statement: For every EthLib input byte array and Lengths value, the integer represented by compute output is base^exponent modulo modulus, or zero when the decoded modulus is zero, using the model input offsets and zero-padding semantics.

details: The property concerns the pure compute helper with the supplied Lengths record, not the entire precompile call.
Local statements and proof bodies were inspected. A complete transitive dependency and axiom audit was not performed.

limitations: The proof does not assert Osaka gas-accounting, exceptional-halt, input-length validation or EVM state-transition correctness.
EthLib describes a BPO2-oriented model; only the modular-exponentiation output behavior was compared with the pinned Osaka source. No cross-fork conformance or client refinement is claimed.

architectureEdges.label: Data availability
architectureEdges.explanation: Fulu on_block requires is_data_available before accepting the block and its post-state.

architectureEdges.label: State transition
architectureEdges.explanation: on_block validates the block using the state transition before storing its post-state.

architectureEdges.label: Epoch processing
architectureEdges.explanation: Fulu process_epoch invokes inherited justification and finalization.

architectureEdges.label: Hash-tree roots
architectureEdges.explanation: State transition checks the block's state root using hash_tree_root.

architectureEdges.label: Signatures
architectureEdges.explanation: Signature validation and RANDAO processing call BLS verification.

architectureEdges.label: Block delivery
architectureEdges.explanation: Consensus block reception feeds on_block. An interface arrow points from the sender to the receiving role.

architectureEdges.label: SSZ-Snappy
architectureEdges.explanation: Consensus messages use SSZ-Snappy encoding.

architectureEdges.label: Cell proof checks
architectureEdges.explanation: Data column validation calls verify_cell_kzg_proof_batch.

architectureEdges.label: Data columns
architectureEdges.explanation: Gossip and Req/Resp deliver data-column sidecars to availability processing.

architectureEdges.label: Post-state
architectureEdges.explanation: Lstar on_block runs state_transition and advances its checkpoint store from the post-state.

architectureEdges.label: Checkpoint updates
architectureEdges.explanation: Attestation processing updates checkpoint values under strict slot guards.

architectureEdges.label: Hash-tree roots
architectureEdges.explanation: State and block-header processing use SSZ hash_tree_root.

architectureEdges.label: Block signatures
architectureEdges.explanation: Lstar on_block verifies signatures before the state transition.

architectureEdges.label: Public keys
architectureEdges.explanation: Signature verification reconstructs XMSS public keys and message bindings for the aggregate.

architectureEdges.label: Message roots
architectureEdges.explanation: SSZ roots of attestation data and blocks bind the aggregate proof to its messages.

architectureEdges.label: Tree hashing
architectureEdges.explanation: The XMSS Merkle tree uses PoseidonXmss to hash tree layers.

architectureEdges.label: Block delivery
architectureEdges.explanation: The sync service routes gossip blocks to head sync and calls the fork's on_block.

architectureEdges.label: SSZ-Snappy
architectureEdges.explanation: The pinned Lstar networking topics name SSZ-Snappy payload encoding.

architectureEdges.label: Execute transactions
architectureEdges.explanation: Osaka apply_body and process_transaction execute bytecode via the interpreter.

architectureEdges.label: State / receipt roots
architectureEdges.explanation: Block validation compares computed state, transaction and receipt roots.

architectureEdges.label: Chain synchronization
architectureEdges.explanation: ETH retrieves execution headers and bodies for execution; it does not choose consensus finality.

architectureEdges.label: EVM bytecode
architectureEdges.explanation: Compiler to target: solc emits bytecode during development. Execution does not invoke the compiler.
